name: Uterine fibroid embolization
city_blurb: Uterine fibroid embolization (UFE) is a less invasive procedure for fibroids that cause heavy periods, pain, or pressure, and you keep your uterus.

finder.title: Find a doctor for uterine fibroid embolization (UFE)
about: Uterine fibroid embolization (UFE) is for fibroids that cause heavy periods, pain, or pressure. It’s a minimally invasive procedure: a doctor works through a small puncture in the wrist or groin and cuts down the blood going to the fibroids, so they shrink over time. You keep your uterus. Talk to a doctor about whether it’s right for you.
sources: Cochrane systematic review of embolization versus surgery for fibroids
CIRSE standards of practice on uterine artery embolisation (van Overhagen and Reekers, 2015)
ACR Appropriateness Criteria: Management of Uterine Fibroids (2023)

animation.alt: A swollen uterus with large fibroids. A thin tube delivers tiny beads or particles to the arteries feeding them. The fibroids and uterus then shrink.
animation.route_text: The tube goes in at the wrist or groin. This drawing shows the wrist.
caps: Fibroids can make the uterus large and swollen. A rich blood supply feeds them.
A thin tube goes through a tiny skin nick in the wrist or groin. Tiny beads or particles block the blood flow to the fibroids.
Without blood flow, the fibroids shrink over time. The uterus gets smaller, and most women feel much better.

name: Prostate artery embolization
city_blurb: Prostate artery embolization (PAE) is for an enlarged prostate that causes urinary problems, like going often, getting up at night, or a weak stream.

finder.title: Find a doctor for prostate artery embolization (PAE)
about: Prostate artery embolization (PAE) is for an enlarged prostate that causes urinary problems, like going often, getting up at night, or a weak stream. It’s a minimally invasive procedure: a doctor works through a small puncture in the wrist or groin and cuts down the blood going to the prostate, so it shrinks over time. Talk to a doctor about whether it’s right for you.
sources: American Urological Association guideline on benign prostatic hyperplasia (2026 update), as reported by the Society of Interventional Radiology (2026-06-18)
top: Shrink an enlarged prostate without surgery
Prostate artery embolization works through a small puncture in the wrist or groin.

animation.alt: An enlarged prostate squeezes the urine tube. A thin tube delivers tiny beads or particles to the prostate arteries. The prostate shrinks, and urine flows more easily.
animation.route_text: The tube goes in at the wrist or groin. This drawing shows the wrist.
caps: An enlarged prostate squeezes the tube that carries urine. The bladder stays full, and urine only trickles out.
A thin tube goes through a small puncture in the wrist or groin. Tiny beads or particles slow the blood flow to the prostate.
With less blood flow, the prostate shrinks over time. The urine tube opens up, and urine flows more easily.

name: Genicular artery embolization
city_blurb: Genicular artery embolization (GAE) is for knee pain from arthritis that hasn’t gotten better with other treatments.

finder.title: Find a doctor for genicular artery embolization (GAE)
about: Genicular artery embolization (GAE) is for knee pain from arthritis that hasn’t gotten better with other treatments. It’s a minimally invasive procedure: a doctor works through a small puncture in an artery and cuts down the extra blood flow that feeds inflammation in the knee, which can ease the pain. It’s a newer option. Talk to a doctor about whether it’s right for you.
sources: Society of Interventional Radiology position statement on genicular artery embolization (JVIR, 2026)
top: A newer option for knee arthritis pain, without surgery
Genicular artery embolization works through a small puncture and can ease the pain.

animation.alt: A swollen, painful knee with extra small blood vessels. A thin tube delivers tiny particles to those vessels. The swelling calms, and the knee moves.
animation.route_text: The tube goes in through a small puncture, here at the groin, and travels to the knee.
caps: With knee arthritis, the joint gets swollen and painful. Extra small blood vessels feed that swelling, and bending hurts.
A thin tube goes through a small puncture to the small blood vessels around the knee. Tiny particles cut the extra blood flow.
With less blood flow, the swelling can calm down. That can ease the pain. The arthritis itself is still there.

name: Pelvic vein treatment
city_blurb: A doctor guides a thin tube into the wide pelvic veins. Tiny coils, plugs, or a medicine close those veins. If a large vein in the pelvis is squeezed, a doctor can place a stent, a small mesh tube, to hold it open.

name: Hemorrhoid artery embolization
city_blurb: Hemorrhoid artery embolization (HAE) treats bleeding hemorrhoids without surgery. A thin tube goes through a tiny skin nick in the wrist or groin. Tiny coils or beads block the arteries feeding the hemorrhoids, so they bleed less. Most people go home the same day.

finder.title: Find a doctor for hemorrhoid embolization

animation.alt: A bleeding hemorrhoid just inside the bottom. A thin tube places tiny coils or beads in the arteries feeding it. The bleeding stops, and the hemorrhoid settles.
animation.route_text: The tube goes in at the wrist or groin. This drawing shows the wrist.
caps: Hemorrhoids are swollen veins just inside the bottom. Arteries from above bring them blood, and they can bleed.
A thin tube goes through a tiny skin nick in the wrist or groin. Tiny coils or beads block the arteries feeding the hemorrhoids.
With less blood flowing in, the hemorrhoids bleed less. They may shrink a little. For some people, bleeding comes back later.
